text: The legacy criteria AC3 and AC7 are kept word for word as the record of intent, and the deliverable proved instead is the publish state of measure_publish inside rwb_reporting: PUBLISHED with the freshness stamp and the two counts, or HELD with the reason, the alert and the resend by the next run; no lake client, no INT-19 extract and no trailer is built.
why: Arch v5 removes the data lake, INT-19 and INT-20 (DP-17, ADR-018) while two criteria owned by this story assert the extract, its trailer and the lake hold, and a worker may neither rewrite a legacy criterion nor invent a destination.
read: Sections 2, 4, 5, 7, 8, 12.3 and 17 of the APP story, sections 12.3 and 19 of the CON story and sections 3, 12.3 and 13 of the OPS story state that the publish and the hold survive as a row of measure_publish and the freshness stamp of the read model, that no lake path exists, and that the OPS boundary assertion fails a release that adds one.
applied_in: APP sections 2, 4, 5, 7, 8, 12.3, 14, 17, 19; CON sections 12.3, 14, 19; OPS sections 3, 12.3, 13, 19
confirm: Solution architect and the business owner of the reporting feature
impact: The baseline can be published and held inside the service on Day 1; whether any reporting extract is rebuilt for a client is left open and no story builds one

text: The two rows this run consumes from rwb-source-data, the payments since entry and the daily completeness gate, are declared as class C consumed rows in 12.2 with their fakes and are added to the dependency map of the wave, while the metadata C row keeps the two rwb-case rows the plan gives.
why: The run cannot compute realized recovery or refuse a stale baseline without those two rows, and the plan's C row does not carry them.
read: APP section 12.2 lists the payments read and the freshness read with their owner and their fake, sections 3 and 13 name them, and the CON declares the same two rows; the metadata is unchanged.
confirm: Solution architect and the owner of rwb-source-data
impact: The story starts on Day 1 against the two fakes; the dependency map under-reports two rows until it is corrected

text: The definition load of table measure_definition is declared as the reference-load element of this service on its own base, with Reference data right C and the all-or-nothing rule, while the list values stay on the reference-data contract of rwb-case.
why: The table is P9's own in rwb_reporting while the reference-data framework is rwb-case's, and no source gives the P9 operation, so the load cannot run on the rwb-case path.
read: APP sections 4 and 12.1 and CON section 12.1 declare the element with the placeholder, and the CON AC4 gives its right and its messages.
confirm: Solution architect and the owner of rwb-case
impact: The reference data administrator can load a definition on Day 1; the owner of the framework may move the operation later

text: These three stories declare no published event and no consumed event; the service topic stays as the platform provisions it and the event that the wave 1 harness expects is recorded as an owner decision, not invented here.
why: The Ownership Map gives rwb-reporting no event and the pattern set of the key carries no outbox library row, while the harness names rwb.reporting.ReportPublished.v1.
read: Sections 12.3 and 12.4 of the APP and CON stories are None with the reason, section 19 of both names the decision as out of scope, and the OPS release assertion fails a build that adds an event or a consumer group.
applied_in: APP sections 12.3, 12.4, 19; CON sections 12.3, 12.4, 19; OPS sections 12.3, 12.4, 17
confirm: Solution architect, platform event owner and the wave 1 harness owner
impact: No event is built or declared; the harness waits on the reads and the freshness stamp, and a later story would carry a freshness event if the owner wants one

text: The measures read is declared on the reporting base in the wave 1 contract for the harness and the catalog consumer, while its dashboard use, its filters, the Power BI data set and SCR-37 stay RWB-P9-E2009-APP's, and the way a reporting client reaches the snapshot is left open.
why: The legacy story assigns the operation to Epic 2 while the Ownership Map gives it to this service and the harness calls it; with no lake, no source says how Power BI refreshes.
read: APP section 12.1 declares the operation with the TSD shape and names E2 as the dashboard's owner, CON section 12.1 does the same, and both stories keep the dashboard and its data set out of scope.
confirm: Solution architect and the reporting business owner
impact: The harness and the catalog consumer are unblocked in wave 1; the report connection is settled with the PRD

text: approved_by is declared and typed uuid as TSD P9 T3.1 types it, and the legacy approver reference TRB-0001 is carried as a comment on the element and as a test fixture, never as the column type.
why: The TSD types the column uuid while the legacy criterion and the FSD name a reference, and no source says which reference a definition row stores.
read: CON AC2 and section 11 declare the type and the comment, APP AC1 keeps both legacy values verbatim, and no fixture asserts a uuid that no source gives.
confirm: Data steward and the owner of the role model
impact: The table can be built with the documented type; the stored value of the approver is confirmed before the load is used in SIT

text: The definitions read is declared as GET /api/recovery/reporting/v1/measure-definitions with the query parameter onDate and a definition list answer, and the path and the field list are marked as this baseline's declaration until the P3 team confirms them.
why: RWB-P3-E1013-APP consumes the definitions in force across a service boundary, and no source gives the path or the shape of the operation.
read: CON AC1, AC6 and section 12.1 declare the operation, APP section 12.1 consumes it as provided, and CON section 12.8 says the fake carries the placeholder.
confirm: Solution architect and the owner of rwb-case
impact: The P3 story and the wave 1 harness build against the declared shape on Day 1

text: The run of JOB-15 has one trigger, the Temporal Schedule at 01:30 Asia/Bangkok registered by the deployment story, and no Airflow call is wired to it; the legacy job ID JOB-15 is kept in the run record and on SCR-44.
why: DP-10 replaces the Quartz row with a Schedule in the owning service, while Architecture v5 slide 9 describes an Airflow chain that triggers report extracts, and two triggers for one run would publish a date twice.
read: APP and CON section 12.6 declare the one Schedule and its policy, and OPS AC3 asserts one registration, no Quartz row and no second Schedule.
applied_in: APP sections 4, 12.6, 19; CON section 12.6; OPS sections 4, 7, 12.6, 19
confirm: Solution architect and the batch and scheduling owner
impact: One run per business date in wave 1; any later extract trigger is raised as its own change

text: Every alert threshold, channel and owner of this capability is a catalogue row or a values-file entry, the failed-run target is the 15 minutes of NFR-068, and the held publish is the one caller of MSG-GEN-006 now that no lake exists.
why: NFR-067 and NFR-068 require monitoring and an alert to a named owner within a target, and no source gives a threshold, a channel or the expected minutes of the job.
read: OPS sections 3, 4, 8, 13 and 14 keep every value out of the chart and name the held publish as the caller of MSG-GEN-006.
confirm: DevOps team and the operations owner of the reporting capability
impact: The alerts can be rehearsed with synthetic metrics; the values are set per environment without a code change

text: The three tables, their unique keys and the frozen-row trigger are carried by the app story's migration V1013__measures.sql in the per-service Flyway sequence, and the deployment story replays the same sequence before the release is ready.
why: No DB story sits in this key's story set while DP-15 gives every service its own sequence and the legacy story owns the migration of both of its tables.
read: APP sections 11 and 13 name the migration and its objects, OPS section 13 replays it and AC1 asserts it is idempotent and that the trigger exists.
confirm: ACE team and the solution architect
impact: The schema exists for the first release without a separate DB story; a later DB story would take the DDL without changing these two

text: The release date 30 November 2026 is copied unchanged and marked tentative, the disposition Split (rework), the build status Not started, the status Draft (realignment v1) and the PRD reference Pending (C1) stand as the plan states them, and the In-review status of the FSD P9 v3 and the TSD P9 v2 and the absent human approval are not preconditions of this story.
why: The run carries no approvals and the plan fixes these values, so a worker records the default and continues rather than stopping the stage.
read: The metadata table of the three stories carries the values with the date marked (tentative), and each story states that no approval is needed to build against a Draft contract baseline.
applied_in: Metadata of the APP, CON and OPS stories; APP section 3
impact: The three stories can start on Day 1 and the status is realigned when the approvals arrive
